findings.where: Where we're starting: the three destination cards (Canggu, Uluwatu, Kuta Lombok) and their 'Best hostels >' lines, at both widths
findings.fault: The cards and their 'Best hostels >' lines are styled as links: link colour, a chevron, a raised card box and a hover rule. The DOM says all three are static, so a click does nothing. Sending visitors to the destination guides is one of the three jobs this page has, and nothing on the page reaches a guide. 'Explore destinations' only scrolls down to these dead cards.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker who wants to see the Canggu hostels, taps the card or 'Best hostels', and nothing happens. They assume the site is broken or empty, which matters most on a pre-launch page that is trying to earn trust.

findings.where: Nav 'How we rank' (desktop and phone menu) and the footer's 'How we rank', 'Privacy', 'Terms' and 'Report content'
findings.fault: Every one of these links points back to this same page. 'How we rank' is the proof behind the hero's 'ranks on merit alone' claim, and the legal links are where a cautious visitor checks who runs the site. All of them go nowhere.
findings.who_objects: A visitor deciding whether to hand over their email for launch news, who checks the merit-ranking claim or the privacy terms first and finds nothing behind them. The founder would object too, since the brand says 'rankings and scoring methods are published'.

findings.where: Nav bar: 'How we rank' underlined, 'Destinations' not
findings.fault: Only one of the two nav links is underlined. Visitors read that as the current-page marker, which is wrong here: this is the homepage. The brand's own convention also runs the other way, with the current page dropping its underline for semibold.
findings.who_objects: A visitor reading the nav would think they are on the ranking page, or that the two links do different kinds of things.

findings.where: Destination cards: border, shadow and type, at both widths
findings.fault: The cards have a thick purple border that is in no brand colour, a heavy soft shadow at rest, and monospace (typewriter-style) type for the island eyebrows and city names. The brand specifies white cards with a thin sand border, borders before shadows ('nothing sits at rest under a heavy shadow'), and Quicksand/Nunito Sans. The cards look like a different site, or like an unstyled draft.
findings.who_objects: The founder, whose brand sheet sets the card, the palette and the two typefaces. A visitor would also object, because the typewriter names and violet frames read as unfinished just where the page asks them to pick a place.

findings.where: 'Where we're starting' heading against the hero, desktop above all
findings.fault: The section heading is set far larger than anything in the hero: at 1440 px it fills the lower half of the first screen and most of the next. It outweighs the hero's message and its coral action, and pushes the destination cards below the first screen. A squint makes a section label the loudest thing on the page.
findings.who_objects: A first-time visitor scanning the page, whose eye goes to a label rather than to what Manta is and what to do. The founder would object too, since the coral action is meant to be the loudest object in the view.

findings.where: Hero: the eyebrow line 'The better way to find hostels in Indonesia.' above the large 'MantaHostels' wordmark
findings.fault: The line that says what the product is gets small type, while the brand name, already shown in the nav, takes the headline size. The page's message ends up in the least prominent text of the hero.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker giving the page five seconds on a phone. They see the name twice but have to read the small print to learn what it is.

findings.where: Hero buttons: the coral 'Email luc@mantahostels.com for launch news' and the outline 'Explore destinations'
findings.fault: The two buttons have different shapes. The coral one is a full pill and the outline one is a square-cornered box, while the brand gives every control an 8px corner. On the phone the coral label is a whole sentence with an email address in it, and it wraps to two lines inside the pill.
findings.who_objects: The founder, whose control radius is set. A phone visitor also has to read a two-line sentence to find out what the main button does.

findings.where: Desktop: hero text column against the nav wordmark and the 'Where we're starting' section
findings.fault: The hero text starts at about x=424, but the nav wordmark, the section heading and the cards all start at x=195. The hero floats off the page's left edge with no edge of its own to align to.
findings.who_objects: A desktop visitor would sense the page as slightly unassembled. A designer would notice that the edge breaks between the first two screens.

findings.where: Footer line 'Launching across Indonesia · piloting now in Bali' against 'Where we're starting', which lists Kuta Lombok
findings.fault: The footer says the pilot is in Bali only, but the section above lists a Lombok destination as a starting point. The two statements about the launch's scope disagree.
findings.who_objects: A visitor planning a Lombok hop, who cannot tell whether Lombok is covered yet.

findings.where: The whole page: trust and who is behind it
findings.fault: The page has no proof and does not say who is behind Manta. There is no named person beyond the 'luc@' in the email address, and none of the real groundwork is shown. The page asks for an email on the strength of one claim, 'ranks on merit alone', and the link that would back that claim is dead.
findings.who_objects: A wary backpacker, who sees an unknown brand ask for their email with no sign of who runs it or what has actually been done.
